The Recruiting Partners Program is a partnership between employers and the College of Engineering.
It provides strategic assistance with recruiting, enhanced access to target populations, and increased opportunities for visibility.
The program costs $10,000 per fiscal year (July 1–June 30).
Program benefits include personalized assistance, priority access to interview space, and access to student organizations.
The Engineering/EECS Affiliates Program is a collaborative program between Engineering Career Resources & Employer Relations and the School of Electrical Engineering and Computer Science (EECS).
It aims to maximize connections between EECS students and employers.
The program costs $15,000 per fiscal year (July 1–June 30).
Program benefits include personalized assistance, placement at the annual School of EECS Day, and priority access to interview space.

The Industrial and Professional Advisory Council (IPAC) is a select group of representatives from industry, government agencies, academia, and the profession.
IPAC advises the College of Engineering on academic issues and current trends in engineering.

Penn State's IP policies aim to remove impediments to enable a free exchange of ideas and provide flexibility for faculty and students working with industry sponsors.
